STEP 3 - Items: One apple (whole, skin on, no visible sauce or oil).

STEP 4 - Area: The apple's top-down footprint is about 7 x 6.5 cm, roughly 36 cm^2, which is about 11% of the plate's ~320 cm^2 area.

STEP 5 - Volume: Apple is roughly ellipsoidal, so the outer envelope is about 36 cm^2 x 6.5 cm height ≈ 230 ml (a medium apple of about 180-200 ml actual volume is consistent with this).

STEP 6 - Grams: Whole fruit has a bulk density near 0.8-0.9 g/ml when treated as a solid, but the instruction gives cut fruit 0.5-0.7 g/ml. A whole apple is solid, so I use the upper end: 230 ml x 0.85 ≈ 195 g. A medium apple typically weighs about 180-200 g, which agrees.

STEP 7 - Energy: Apple, raw, about 52 kcal per 100 g. 195 g x 0.52 ≈ 101 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: One medium apple weighing about 195 g and about 100 kcal is plausible for what is visible. There is no other food on the plate.
